metadata.rules_text:
- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast periods; model tends to overshoot after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- When sentiment history is uniformly zero, model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices; apply downward adjustment of 3–5% for 30-day forecasts.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a peak, model often fails to recognize the turning point — reduce forecast peak by 10–15% in subsequent periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if model shows persistent upward trend beyond 10–12 days, consider tapering slope or adding decay factor.
- Sentiment context (if available) should override pure historical pattern — if sentiment shifts to negative or uncertain, reduce forecast volatility and shift mean toward lower range.
- Model underestimates volatility in low-sentiment periods; add 1–2% noise buffer to forecast range if sentiment remains flat for >10 days.
